(1) a principled way of learning domain-invariant representations can be used to train a perception model on the synthetic data alone; (2) the domain gap can be reduced with a simple data augmentation scheme that samples from the simulator; and (3) the type of variations in the synthetic data matters for the final performance of the model.

(i)  we can use synthetic data alone for training perception models with a small reality gap; (ii) the domain adaptation technique can be used to compensate for the variations in the simulator; (iii) the simulator variations that are not accounted for in the adaptation technique are the ones that matter for the performance on real data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a simulator is not a silver bullet and that the domain gap is still a significant challenge.
the simulator is a powerful tool that should not be underestimated, but that it should be used with care.
